segments.en: Okay.

segments.zh: 他或她是一个会帮助您将汽油放入车内的人。

segments.zh: 所以服务员是一个几乎像助手或助手的人。

segments.en: You can have a bathroom attendant, someone who gives you a towel after you wash your hands.
segments.zh: 你可以有一个浴室服务员，在你洗手后给你一条毛巾的人。

segments.en: Yeah, so gas station attendant.

segments.zh: 我还做了调查，查到经理们的名字，这样求职信里就能直接称呼他们。

segments.en: And you know, I can be charming in interviews.
segments.zh: 而且你知道，我面试时可是很有魅力的。

segments.zh: 就像那些大人物成功之前一样，先从简单、基层的工作做起。

segments.zh: 那么，我们为什么不在语言外卖中看看其中的一些。

segments.en: The first phrase we have today is one that's very important when you're looking for a job.
segments.zh: 我们今天的第一个短语在你找工作时非常重要。

segments.en: It's called job listing or job listings here.
segments.zh: 它在这里称为工作列表或工作列表。

segments.en: Okay, job listings.
segments.zh: 好的，工作列表。

segments.en: And this is really common before the internet existed.
segments.zh: 在互联网存在之前，这真的很常见。

segments.en: You would have the listings in your local newspaper, right?
segments.zh: 你会在当地的报纸上看到列表，对吧？

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: In the movies, you always had the person sitting with the newspaper circling the potential jobs.
segments.zh: 在电影中，你总是有一个坐在报纸上盘旋潜在工作的人。

segments.en: Right, with a red marker.
segments.zh: 对，用红色标记。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: But now that we have the internet, you have lots of websites that have job listings.
segments.zh: 但是现在我们有了互联网，你有很多网站有工作列表。

segments.en: And so a job listing is literally a list of jobs that are available.
segments.zh: 因此，工作列表实际上是一个可用的工作列表。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So you look through the job listings.
segments.zh: 因此，您查看工作列表。

segments.en: Maybe you found one that's interesting.
segments.zh: 也许你找到了一款很有趣的东西。

segments.en: There's an email address.
segments.zh: 有一个电子邮件地址。

segments.en: So what do they ask for?
segments.zh: 那么他们要求什么？

segments.en: They ask you to send in your resume.
segments.zh: 他们要求您发送简历。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: A resume is very important when you're looking for a job.
segments.zh: 当您在找工作时，简历非常重要。

segments.en: It's a document.
segments.zh: 这是一份文件。

segments.en: It's a piece of paper that tells someone all of the work that you've done before, your job experiences, and it tells them where you went to school and what your qualifications are.
segments.zh: 这是一张纸，告诉某人你以前做过的所有工作，你的工作经历，它告诉他们你在哪里上学以及你的资格是什么。

segments.en: So it's a summary of your work life.
segments.zh: 所以这是你工作生活的总结。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And that's why it's called a resume, right?
segments.zh: 这就是为什么它被称为简历，对吧？

segments.en: It's pretty much a summary of your work life, as you say.
segments.zh: 正如你所说，这几乎是你工作生活的总结。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And a different one, sometimes people use this, is a CV, curriculum vitae, and that's an academic summary of your life.
segments.zh: 另一个，有时人们使用它，是一份简历，简历，这是对你生活的学术总结。

segments.en: So you have the work summary and the study summary.
segments.zh: 所以你有工作总结和学习总结。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: So if you send in your resume, what's recommended is that you attach it with a cover letter.
segments.zh: 因此，如果您发送简历，建议您将其附有求职信。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Well, cover letter, you know the word letter.
segments.zh: 好吧，求职信，你知道字母这个词。

segments.en: It's something that you write to somebody else.
segments.zh: 这是你写给别人的东西。

segments.en: But a cover letter is like a cover for your resume.
segments.zh: 但是求职信就像你简历的封面。

segments.en: It's a letter where you explain to the future boss or future employer what exactly you want and how this job is going to help you get it.
segments.zh: 这是一封信，您向未来的老板或未来的雇主解释您到底想要什么以及这份工作将如何帮助您获得它。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So that's basically a small little introduction to yourself, right?
segments.zh: 所以这基本上是对自己的一个小小的介绍，对吧？

segments.en: Before they read your resume, who you are, what you're looking for, maybe very quickly.
segments.zh: 在他们阅读您的简历之前，您是谁，您正在寻找什么，也许很快。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So you can say, Hi, my name is Catherine.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说，嗨，我的名字是凯瑟琳。

segments.en: I'm very motivated and excited to have the opportunity to talk to you about why I'm a skilled employee and why I will benefit your company.
segments.zh: 我非常有动力和兴奋有机会与您讨论我为什么是一名熟练的员工以及为什么我会使您的公司受益。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So you've sent in your resume and your cover letter.
segments.zh: 所以你已经发送了你的简历和求职信。

segments.en: And well, maybe you're looking to get into a career as a gas station attendant.
segments.zh: 好吧，也许您正在寻找作为加油站服务员的职业。

segments.en: So what's the difference between job and career?
segments.zh: 那么工作和职业有什么区别呢？

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And this is very interesting because in many languages, there is a similar word, which for example, in Spanish is carrera, right?
segments.zh: 这很有趣，因为在许多语言中，有一个相似的词，例如，在西班牙语中是卡雷拉，对吧？

segments.en: And that means like a profession.
segments.zh: 这意味着像一个职业。

segments.en: So many people translate it literally as career, but it's not the right word.
segments.zh: 很多人从字面上翻译它是职业，但它不是正确的词。

segments.en: What is a career?
segments.zh: 什么是职业？

segments.en: A career I think of as a long term goal.
segments.zh: 我认为的职业生涯是一个长期目标。

segments.en: A career is your profession.
segments.zh: 职业就是你的职业。

segments.en: It's the name you give yourself.
segments.zh: 这是你给自己起的名字。

segments.en: But a job is a position in a company from one time to another.
segments.zh: 但一份工作是一家公司从一次到另一个职位的职位。

segments.en: So for example, my job here is host of EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 因此，例如，我在这里的工作是 Host EnglishPod。

segments.en: But maybe in the future, I will have a media career.
segments.zh: 但也许在未来，我将拥有媒体职业。

segments.en: That means that my job or jobs will have to do with this profession.
segments.zh: 这意味着我的工作或工作将与这个职业有关。

segments.en: It's kind of a bigger thing, a longer thing.
segments.zh: 这是一件更大的事情，更长的事情。

segments.en: So maybe you can think of it this way.
segments.zh: 所以也许你可以这样想。

segments.en: A career is like, as you say, bigger picture, like the macro category, right?
segments.zh: 正如你所说，一个职业就像宏观类别一样，对吧？

segments.en: You're into media and television, for example.
segments.zh: 例如，你喜欢媒体和电视。

segments.en: And your job specifically is a podcast host.
segments.zh: 你的工作特别是播客主持人。

segments.en: But in the future, maybe I want to have a different job in this career and move into production and be a TV producer.
segments.zh: 但在未来，也许我想在这个职业中有一份不同的工作，进入制作行业并成为一名电视制作人。

segments.en: So that's a part of my career path.
segments.zh: 所以这是我职业道路的一部分。

segments.en: I can move forward.
segments.zh: 我可以继续前进。

segments.en: So career is very important word.
segments.zh: 所以职业是非常重要的词。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we've taken a look at a couple of great words.
segments.zh: 所以我们看了几个很棒的词。

segments.en: Why don't we listen to our dialogue again and we'll be back in a bit.
segments.zh: 我们为什么不再听一次我们的对话，我们会回来的。

segments.en: I've even done my research and found the names of the managers so I can address the letters personally.
segments.zh: 我还做了调查，查到经理们的名字，这样求职信里就能直接称呼他们。

segments.en: And you know, I can be charming in interviews.
segments.zh: 而且你知道，我面试时可是很有魅力的。

segments.en: Goodbye my penniless days.
segments.zh: 再见我身无分文的日子。

segments.en: Hello salary and a career.

segments.en: Ben, we're 15.
segments.zh: 本，我们才15岁。

segments.en: What kind of job are you looking for?

segments.en: Oh, just for a position as a gas station attendant.
segments.zh: 哦，只是为了一个加油站服务员的职位。

segments.en: You know, starting at a simple lowly job, just like all the greats before they made it big in the world.
segments.zh: 你知道，从一个简单的低级工作开始，就像所有伟大的人在世界上大放异彩之前一样。

segments.en: But I'm just in it for the money, right?
segments.zh: 但我只是为了钱，对吧？

segments.en: How else am I going to be able to afford to keep taking Angela to the movies?
segments.zh: 不然我怎么能负担得起继续带安吉拉去看电影？

segments.en: Besides, I love the smell of gasoline.
segments.zh: 此外，我喜欢汽油的气味。

segments.en: Don't you?
segments.zh: 你不是吗？

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So now we have lined up for you three key phrases that we found in this dialogue.
segments.zh: 所以现在我们已经为你排好了我们在这次对话中找到的三个关键短语。

segments.en: So let's take a look at those now in Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 所以让我们来看看现在在 Fluency Builder 中的那些。

segments.zh: 流利表达。

segments.en: This first one's a great phrase.

segments.en: It's going to make you sound very fluent in English if you use it.
segments.zh: 如果你使用它，它会让你听起来非常流利。

segments.en: We say in the market for.
segments.zh: 我们在市场上说。

segments.en: I'm in the market for a new job.
segments.zh: 我在市场上寻找新工作。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So this person is looking for a new job.
segments.zh: 所以这个人正在寻找新的工作。

segments.en: He is in the market for.
segments.zh: 他在市场上。

segments.en: I could also say, I'm in the market for a new house.
segments.zh: 我也可以说，我在市场上寻找新房子。

segments.en: Marco, do you know any good real estate agents?
segments.zh: 马可，你知道有什么好的房地产经纪人吗？

segments.en: So what does that mean if you say I'm in the market for a new job or you're in the market for a new house?
segments.zh: 那么，如果您说我在市场上寻找新工作，或者您在市场上寻找新房子，这意味着什么？

segments.en: I am right now actively looking for this thing.
segments.zh: 我现在正在积极寻找这个东西。

segments.en: I really want one.
segments.zh: 我真的很想要一份。

segments.en: You're available.
segments.zh: 你有空。

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So I'm in the market for a new job.
segments.zh: 所以我在市场上寻找新工作。

segments.en: I'm in the market for a new car.

segments.en: It means the market is the marketplace.

segments.en: Right, right.

segments.zh: 有时你可以在电影中看到它。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Do you know any nice guys?
segments.zh: 你认识什么好人吗？

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So you're in the market.
segments.zh: 所以你在市场上。

segments.en: You're looking for a job.
segments.zh: 你在找工作。

segments.en: And well, if you're qualified, it will be a piece of cake to find a new job.
segments.zh: 好吧，如果你有资格，找到新工作将是小菜一碟。

segments.en: Isn't this a delicious phrase?
segments.zh: 这不是一个美味的短语吗？

segments.en: So piece of cake, you think what does cake have to do with anything?
segments.zh: 所以一块蛋糕，你认为蛋糕和任何东西有什么关系？

segments.en: Well, cake, this is a way to say something is easy.
segments.zh: 好吧，蛋糕，这是说某事很容易的一种方式。

segments.en: Okay, so it's really easy.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以真的很简单。

segments.en: This often happens in our office actually, because you and I understand computers, but we work with someone who has a hard time with computers.
segments.zh: 这实际上经常发生在我们的办公室，因为您和我了解计算机，但我们与计算机工作困难的人一起工作。

segments.en: And she's like, oh, it doesn't work.
segments.zh: 她就像，哦，它不起作用。

segments.en: And we're like, it's a piece of cake.
segments.zh: 我们就像，它是小菜一碟。

segments.en: It's a piece of cake.
segments.zh: 这是一块蛋糕。

segments.en: It's so easy.
segments.zh: 太容易了。

segments.en: Why is this hard?

segments.en: So a piece of cake is a way to say something simple.
segments.zh: 所以一块蛋糕是一种说简单的方式。

segments.en: And it's a very, very, very common phrase.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常、非常、非常常见的短语。

segments.en: You'll hear it all the time.
segments.zh: 你会一直听到的。

segments.en: A piece of cake, don't worry about it.
segments.zh: 一块蛋糕，不用担心。

segments.en: Piece of cake.
segments.zh: 一块蛋糕。

segments.en: Hey, can you help me out with this thing?
segments.zh: 嘿，你能帮我解决这个问题吗？

segments.en: Sure, it's a piece of cake.
segments.zh: 当然，这是小菜一碟。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And for our last phrase, he was talking about his position as a gas attendant.
segments.zh: 对于我们的最后一句话，他是在谈论他作为燃气服务员的地位。

segments.en: And he said, well, you know, all the greats, all the famous people, they started somewhere before they made it big.
segments.zh: 他说，好吧，你知道，所有伟大的人，所有名人，他们在做大事之前就开始了。

segments.en: What does he mean with they made it big?
segments.zh: 他把它做大是什么意思？

segments.en: Well, the phrase to make it big or in here in the past tense, made it big, means to be successful.
segments.zh: 好吧，把它变大的短语或在这里时时，使它变大，意味着成功。

segments.en: So we're talking about, for example, Albert Einstein.
segments.zh: 所以我们谈论的是，例如，阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦。

segments.en: Albert Einstein worked in the patent office in a clue.
segments.zh: 阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦在专利局工作的线索。

segments.en: He was a clerk in Europe.
segments.zh: 他是欧洲的一名文员。

segments.en: And you know, that's not a very impressive job, but it was a job.
segments.zh: 你知道，这不是一份令人印象深刻的工作，但这是一份工作。

segments.en: And he made it big later on as a physicist.
segments.zh: 他后来成为一名物理学家。

segments.en: And so to make it big is to succeed, to become famous or successful or important.
segments.zh: 因此，要成功，就是成功，成名或成功或重要。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Or sometimes people say, yeah, I made it.
segments.zh: 或者有时人们会说，是的，我做到了。

segments.en: I made it big or I made it in my life.
segments.zh: 我成功了，或者我在我的生活中成功了。

segments.en: And that means that you were successful.
segments.zh: 这意味着你成功了。

segments.en: Or this product is going to make it big.
segments.zh: 或者这个产品会让它变得大。

segments.en: It's going to be really successful.
segments.zh: 它会真正成功。

segments.en: Yeah, that's good.
segments.zh: 是的，这很好。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So it's a key phrase to make it or to make it big.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个关键的短语，让它变大。

segments.en: Why don't we listen to our dialogue for the last time and we'll be back in a little bit.
segments.zh: 为什么我们不听我们最后一次的对话，我们会回来一点。

segments.en: Woohoo!
segments.zh: 好耶！

segments.en: This just might be the start of the rest of my life.
segments.zh: 这可能是我余生的开始。

segments.en: What happened?
segments.zh: 发生什么事了？

segments.en: I'm in the market for a job.
segments.zh: 我正在找工作。

segments.en: I went on a website with hundreds of job listings in the area and browsed through them until I got the names of a few employers I would like to work for.
segments.zh: 我去了一个网站，在该地区有数百个工作列表，并浏览了它们，直到我得到了一些我想为之工作的雇主的名字。

segments.en: I have the resume I wrote for English class last month and a cover letter will be a piece of cake to write.
segments.zh: 我有上个月为英语课写的简历，求职信将是小菜一碟。

segments.en: I've even done my research and found the names of the managers so I can address the letters personally.
segments.zh: 我还做了调查，查到经理们的名字，这样求职信里就能直接称呼他们。

segments.en: And you know, I can be charming in interviews.
segments.zh: 而且你知道，我面试时可是很有魅力的。

segments.en: Goodbye my penniless days.
segments.zh: 再见我身无分文的日子。

segments.en: Hello salary and a career.
segments.zh: 你好薪水和职业。

segments.en: Ben, we're 15.
segments.zh: 本，我们才15岁。

segments.en: What kind of job are you looking for?
segments.zh: 你在找什么样的工作？

segments.en: Oh, just for a position as a gas station attendant.
segments.zh: 哦，只是为了一个加油站服务员的职位。

segments.en: You know, starting at a simple lowly job just like all the greats before they made it big in the world.
segments.zh: 就像那些大人物成功之前一样，先从简单、基层的工作做起。

segments.en: Uh huh.
segments.zh: 嗯哼。

segments.en: But I'm just in it for the money, right?
segments.zh: 但我只是为了钱，对吧？

segments.en: How else am I going to be able to afford to keep taking Angela to the movies?
segments.zh: 不然我怎么能负担得起继续带安吉拉去看电影？

segments.en: Besides, I love the smell of gasoline.
segments.zh: 此外，我喜欢汽油的气味。

segments.en: Don't you?
segments.zh: 你不是吗？

segments.en: All right, so talking about jobs, now I noticed something that in the United States, unlike many other countries, there are no gas station attendants anymore.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以说到工作，现在我注意到在美国，与许多其他国家不同，不再有加油站服务员了。

segments.en: There are.
segments.zh: 有。

segments.en: Touche.
segments.zh: 触摸。

segments.en: There are actually a lot of gas station attendants in New Jersey because it's the law that you cannot pump your own gas.
segments.zh: 实际上，新泽西州有很多加油站服务员，因为这是您无法自燃汽油的法律。

segments.en: You cannot put gas in your own car.
segments.zh: 你不能在自己的车里加油。

segments.en: Why is that?
segments.zh: 为什么会这样？

segments.en: It's a way for the New Jersey government to increase the amount of jobs in the states.
segments.zh: 这是新泽西州政府增加美国就业数量的一种方式。

segments.en: So to create jobs, they made gas station attendants.
segments.zh: 所以为了创造就业机会，他们让加油站服务员。

segments.en: Oh wow.
segments.zh: 哦，哇。

segments.en: Yeah, I've noticed in some states, for example, you just go up to the pump and if you have your credit card, you put in your credit card and you pump your own gas.
segments.zh: 是的，我注意到在某些州，例如，您只需上水泵，如果您有信用卡，您将信用卡放入您的信用卡并抽出自己的汽油。

segments.en: And apparently it also has to do with health issues because people who are working in gas stations tend to have serious health problems later on.
segments.zh: 显然，这也与健康问题有关，因为在加油站工作的人后来往往会出现严重的健康问题。

segments.en: I mean, you're inhaling all these gases from the gasoline.
segments.zh: 我的意思是，你从汽油中吸入了所有这些气体。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: It's very unhealthy.
segments.zh: 这是非常不健康的。

segments.en: And I think that's also very dangerous in some places because gas stations are often robbed because there's only one person and no security sometimes.
segments.zh: 而且我认为这在某些地方也很危险，因为加油站经常被抢劫，因为有时只有一个人，而且有时没有安全保障。

segments.en: So there are some negative parts of being a gas station attendant.
segments.zh: 因此，作为加油站服务员有一些负面影响。

segments.en: But if it's a job and you need a job, it's probably a good one.
segments.zh: 但如果这是一份工作并且你需要一份工作，那可能是一份好工作。

segments.en: Yeah, no, true.
segments.zh: 是的，不，是真的。

segments.en: I actually, I remember seeing Back to the Future when in the 50s, you would pull up to a gas station, somebody would check your tire pressure, they would check your oil and they would clean your windows and it's just like full service when you pulled up to a gas station.
segments.zh: 实际上，我记得在 50 年代回到未来时，你会停下来，有人会检查你的轮胎压力，他们会检查你的油，他们会清理你的窗户，就像你拉到加油站时一样，这就像全方位的服务一样。

segments.en: They might even buy you a beer.
segments.zh: 他们甚至可能给你买啤酒。

segments.en: Alright, so it's really interesting about these positions.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以这些职位真的很有趣。

segments.en: I imagine that in other places, some job positions that maybe we would find a little bit strange or uncommon.
segments.zh: 我想在其他地方，一些工作职位可能我们会觉得有点奇怪或不常见。

segments.en: Absolutely.
segments.zh: 当然。

segments.en: And I encourage everyone today, this is your homework, tell us on EnglishPod.com what is your job and what's your career.
segments.zh: 我今天鼓励大家，这是你的作业，在 Englishpod.com 上告诉我们你的工作是什么，你的职业是什么。

segments.en: What's your job and what's your career.
segments.zh: 你的工作是什么，你的职业是什么。

segments.en: So what's the career you would like to have in the future.
segments.zh: 那么你未来想拥有的职业是什么。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: Alright, so we'll see you guys there.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们会在那里见到你们。

segments.en: Bye everyone.
segments.zh: 大家再见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
